title: Audit Defence and Controversy
answer: Audit defence and controversy covers the work of responding to tax authority inquiries, audits, assessments, appeals, and mutual agreement procedures across jurisdictions. It includes reconstructing tax positions, gathering evidence, managing deadlines, and negotiating or litigating disputes over income tax, VAT, customs, employment taxes, and transfer pricing. sections.body: Audit defence and controversy covers the work of responding to tax authority inquiries, audits, assessments, appeals, and mutual agreement procedures across jurisdictions. It includes reconstructing tax positions, gathering evidence, managing deadlines, and negotiating or litigating disputes over income tax, VAT, customs, employment taxes, and transfer pricing. In practice it sits at the intersection of tax technical knowledge, data engineering, and dispute resolution, because authorities increasingly request structured data rather than paper files. The site's 219 compliance and regulation pages show how often this work overlaps with broader regulatory obligations, from data protection to anti money laundering. AI enters mainly as a way to classify documents, trace transactions, and test the consistency of the positions being defended.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on the taxpayer's core financial and tax systems, including ERP ledgers, tax engines, e invoicing platforms, and document management repositories. Case management tools hold notices, correspondence, deadlines, and workpapers, while secure data rooms and controlled cloud regions handle exchanges with advisers and authorities. Audit trails, access logs, version history, and data residency controls matter because evidence must be traceable and transferable across borders. AI components typically sit alongside these systems as document review engines, optical character recognition, natural language processing, anomaly detection, and knowledge graphs. The infrastructure must support both structured tax data and unstructured evidence such as contracts, emails, and invoices.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A typical matter starts with intake and scoping, where the team identifies the authority, the periods, the taxes, and the legal issues in play. The next step is data collection and reconstruction, pulling transactions from ledgers, contracts, invoices, and correspondence to rebuild the positions under review. AI can help by classifying documents, extracting key terms, building timelines, flagging anomalies, and checking whether the same facts are described consistently across submissions. Human reviewers then test the evidence, assess the strength of each argument, and draft responses, objections, or settlement proposals. Throughout, the method is iterative, because new questions from the authority often require fresh data pulls and revised risk assessments.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk turn on privilege, confidentiality, tax secrecy, data protection, and the rules for cross border data transfer. Evidence provenance is central, so teams need chain of custody, clear versioning, and an audit trail that shows who touched what and when. AI outputs add risk if they are opaque, biased, or hallucinated, so firms typically require human review, documented prompts, and model validation before anything is filed. The site tracks 148 active AI lawsuits, a reminder that disputes over automated decisions and evidence are already real. Professional standards, penalty exposure, and disclosure duties mean that governance is not a back office concern but part of the defence itself.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward more real time reporting, more structured data requests, and more use of AI by tax authorities to select, scope, and test audits. Taxpayers are likely to respond with their own analytics, using AI to monitor controversy risk, prepare evidence packs, and simulate outcomes before negotiations. Cross border disputes and transfer pricing controversies will remain a major source of work, especially as digital taxes and global minimum tax rules mature. The site's 732 AI tools suggest a growing market for document review, case analytics, and drafting support, but audit defence will stay human led because judgment, privilege, and accountability cannot be delegated to a model. Expect continued tension over explainability, data access, and the line between legitimate tax planning and aggressive positions.
